title: Tomographic flow regime vs even-odd effect for the magnetotransport in the Corbino geometry
abstract: In two dimensions, the geometric constraints due to Pauli blocking and conservation laws lead to the even-odd effect exhibited by the electron-electron scattering lengths: electron-electron collisions are more efficient at relaxing the even angular harmonics of the distribution function than the odd ones. Inspired by a recent experiment on the magnetotransport in the Corbino disk geometry, we numerically analyze the electron flows in this geometry across all the regimes.   We predict a clear signature of the even-odd effect - enhancement of the resistance sensitivity $\partial R/\partial(B^2)$ at small magnetic fields $B\rightarrow 0$. This enhancement is most prominent at the crossover from the ballistic to the tomographic regime, and gradually disappears when the temperature is further increased. Our estimates suggest that in the temperature range of the experiment, the effect should be small. This implies that the attribution of the anomalous scaling of the kinematic viscosity, that was observed in the experiment, to the even-odd effect might need more careful consideration.   As a side note, we show how the method of characteristics can be extended to treat the long-lived odd harmonics, which allows one to recast the linearized Boltzmann equation as a system of integral ones.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes electron transport in a Corbino disk geometry by comparing two effects: the tomographic flow regime and the even-odd effect arising from electron-electron scattering. The authors predict that the even-odd effect should manifest as an enhancement in resistance sensitivity at low magnetic fields, providing a diagnostic tool for understanding quantum kinetic phenomena in 2D materials.
main_problem: The paper investigates magnetotransport in the Corbino geometry, comparing the influence of geometric constraints (tomographic flow regime) against intrinsic electron-electron scattering effects (even-odd effect).
main_result: The authors predict a distinct signature of the even-odd effect—an enhancement of $\partial R/\partial(B^2)$ at small magnetic fields ($B 	o 0$)—which is most visible near the crossover from ballistic to tomographic flow.
method: Numerical analysis solving the linearized Boltzmann equation by expanding the distribution function in angular eigenmodes (Fourier series).
model_or_system: The study models two-dimensional electron systems confined to a Corbino disk geometry under an applied magnetic field, using the linearized Boltzmann equation to describe non-equilibrium electron flows.
key_observables: Resistance sensitivity ($\partial R/\partial(B^2)$) at low fields, and dimensionless conductance ($G/G_0$).
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), magnetic field strength ($B$), ratio of scattering rates for even vs. odd harmonics ($\gamma_{e}^{ee}/\gamma_{o}^{ee}$), and the crossover parameter $v_F 	au_{	ext{even}} / r_b$.
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the linearized regime, assuming a degenerate electron gas ($T \ll E_F$), and relies on specific approximations for scattering interactions (e.g., $I_{	ext{ex}} \approx -I_{	ext{dir}}/2$).
figures_summary: Figures show normalized conductance and resistance sensitivity ($\partial R/\partial(B^2)$) as a function of the ratio of Larmor radius to disk size ($r_b/R_L$), demonstrating parameter dependence.
paper_structure: The paper develops theoretical frameworks by deriving scattering rates for odd and even harmonics, solving the linearized Boltzmann equation across different flow regimes (ballistic to tomographic), and finally predicting observable signatures in magnetotransport measurements.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the detailed analysis of non-equilibrium dynamics using the Boltzmann equation and harmonic decomposition touches upon advanced kinetic theory relevant to open quantum systems far from equilibrium.
